v.why: Raising an already large learning rate causes Adam training to diverge, giving large accuracy drops.
At tiny learning rates the network is undertrained in 243 epochs, so increasing lr helps more than elsewhere.
Increasing an already strong L2 penalty causes underfitting with large accuracy losses, while small alpha changes are negligible.
Larger batches reduce gradient noise and stabilize training when the learning rate is too large.
Deeper networks are more prone to divergence at large learning rates.
Extra depth adds capacity and effective step size that help undertrained networks at small learning rates.
Wider layers amplify instability at large learning rates, hurting accuracy.
Lowering an excessively large learning rate rescues diverged training, giving large gains.
Reducing an excessive L2 penalty relieves underfitting, while at small alpha it has almost no effect.
With strong L2, larger batches mean fewer shrinkage steps per epoch, reducing over-regularization.

raw:
Hypotheses drawn from the experiments plus standard MLP/Adam behavior:

1. lr up, cond lr high → lower (divergence at large lr; exps 3, 12, 13, 16, 20).
2. lr up, cond lr low → higher (undertrained at tiny lr; exps 2, 14, 18).
3. alpha up, cond alpha high → lower (strong L2 collapses fit; exps 84, 93–98).
4. batch_size up, cond lr high → higher (larger batches stabilize big steps; exps 23, 33, 35).
5. depth up, cond lr high → lower (deeper nets diverge more at large lr; exps 64, 72, 79).
6. depth up, cond lr low → higher (extra depth helps when undertrained; exps 63, 73, 80).
7. width up, cond lr high → lower (exps 43, 54, 58).
8. lr down, cond lr high → higher (mirror of 1).
9. alpha down, cond alpha high → higher (removing excessive regularization helps).
10. batch_size up, cond alpha high → higher (exps 39, 40; larger batch reduces per-epoch L2 shrinkage steps).
